exposure: Grade/size of subchorionic hematoma (small, medium, large)
Gestational age at SCH detection (<12 weeks vs 12-20 weeks)
cohort: A total of 171 women with singleton pregnancies, 72 of whom had subchorionic hematoma before 20 weeks and between 12 and 20 weeks of gestational age, enrolled between January 2018 and December 2021.
finding: Women with subchorionic hematoma, especially detected between 12 and 20 weeks GA or of medium/large size, face a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes including miscarriage, early preterm birth, premature rupture of membranes, and fetal growth restriction.
gest_age: SCH detected before 20 weeks and between 12 and 20 weeks gestational age; outcomes measured up to gestational age at delivery (mean ~37-39 weeks).
